newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gengold says gold hedging review unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Gengold says gold hedging review unlikely.

text.p: The weaker bullion price and expectations that the rand might stabilise in 1997 was unlikely to force Gencor Ltd to review its gold hedging strategy, Gengold managing director Tom Dale said on Monday.
A steady rand and dull dollar gold price would trim revenues for South African gold mines, possibly worrying some into locking in a better price by implementing more hedge positions.
But asked if Gengold would review its strategy, Dale told Reuters: "I wouldn't think so. We're not natural hedgers like Anglo American. The Beatrix hedge was to protect a specific capital project."
In 1995 Gengold implemented a long-term 90 tonne deal to fund expansion of the No. 3 shaft at Beatrix Mines Ltd.
The hedge cost Beatrix during the December quarter, when the average actual gold price received by the mine in the three months to end-December was 56,095 rand/kg.
The hedged price was 50,763 rand/kg and the lower price put Beatrix's distributable income at 40.34 million rand, compared to 43.9 million rand it would have received at spot gold prices.
"The hedge price increases by 1,000 rand a quarter, so if the gold price doesn't go up this quarter then Beatrix could one of these days be back in the black in its hedge," Dale said.
The expansion at Beatrix had been successful so far and was within budget, Gengold said.
It added that by the end of the March quarter it hoped to have put through 230,000 tonnes of ore per month.
On the generally weaker gold price, Dale said: "It doesn't look as good now as it did for the previous quarter."
Gold was trading around $354.20/50 an ounce on Monday.
